answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a scarce-slot auction mechanism, where each new identity must win limited slots that open each epoch. Each agent submits increasing bids, with the price for a slot starting at 10 tokens but quickly climbing to over 100 tokens as competition rises. This system makes it expensive for attackers trying to forge multiple identities since they face costs exceeding 1,000. Navigating this auction is like traversing an ocean, where each wave represents escalating prices, compelling agents to compose their own sonnet amidst the chaos of the nebula.
